Privacy Friendly & Beautiful/Functional Bible App!! Way to go!!. This app is beautiful, customizable, and has so many features that are great for reading and studying. You can dive deeper into the specific features in the app description.

NOTE:
My highest reason for the 5 star rating (outside of the beauty & functionality) is that this bible app collects no data.

If you are into privacy friendly apps and want to read the Bible, use this app. 

I never gave any thought to how bible apps collect data or if they did because I simply wanted to read the Bible, and the assumption is: the people running said bible app must be good & ethical Christian people and things like “sharing/selling my data” is something I don’t have to worry or even think about. 

Privacy policies on certain bible apps do state that they do collect data and share it with third parties or government etc.

reviews.text:
Simple and Yet Never Lacking. This has been my favorite Bible app since 2013, when I got my first piece of personal technology as a kid. I was trying out other bible apps and none of them are bad by any means but this one executes something better than the rest. Simplicity. When I’m reading the Bible I want it to allow me to do one main thing: read it. This one has never failed to give me the best experience for reading the Bible.

One of my favorite things is the accessibility. Although it’s never necessary for any user to go into the accessibility, it has many options that users can change to their liking. For example, if the default text isn’t sharp enough for you, switch it to a serif font like Times New Roman. There are many other accessibility features as well, so if you don’t like the default feel free to go in and play around until it gives you the best reading experience for you. Personally, that’s a big thing that makes me like this app. I never cared for any Bible app’s default look too much, and now that I’ve changed it I can’t switch back.

I also appreciate the simple highlighting tools. It’s just a two tap process and it highlights the whole verse. It also has a great way of looking up those highlights again. You can pair up highlight colors however you want or not at all if you don’t care, but whenever you go back to look at them, they’re organized by color so if you remember the color you used, you can find it quickly.

The search tool has been one of my favorite features. It has helped me find many verses I remembered the basic idea of, without knowing the full words or reference.

Notes are another thing I think it does well. Most of the time I prefer to take notes on an outside source specifically paper but taking notes in the app is still great. It takes notes in correlation to the open chapter, so it’s not the best for sermons if your pastor wants you to look at multiple verses in different chapters of different books. The great thing about it is searching for notes you’ve taken. It makes it very easy.

The in app purchases are not necessary for users, however, I love the features it brings. My personal favorite is the topical search. Searching the Bible specifically by topic is wonderful. It’s great for learning about specific things, teaching Bible studies, and just overall understanding God’s Word better. There are many other features it adds like commentaries by very scholarly people. Reading the Bible with perspective is very healthy.

Lastly, this app has many versions you can choose from. It does not have NIV, which I’ve always wanted it to have, so if that’s a deal breaker then this isn’t for you. Still, I like having different versions to read from to help me better understand different sections of the Bible that don’t make sense to me at first.

Overall, it’s a great app. There are many features I didn’t cover, but I think if you give it a try, you’ll like it too.

Despite a new update, that is still the case. At this point, I can read a chapter strait through, and can go to previous or next chapter, but that’s about _all I can do. Find a passage in a hurry? No way! Use the study tools? I purchased them, but so far haven’t gotten them to come up. Preferences? I can’t even _get _to them now! If these suggestions were followed, I think that the app would benefit not only VoiceOver users, but also the rest of us . Most customizable bible app on iOS. This app is superb. It is by far the most customizable bible app on the App Store when it comes to formatting. Paragraph kjv? Check. Precise margin adjustments? Check. Fonts, font sizes, margins, line spacing, indentation or not, HIDE VERSE NUMBERS for readability!, customizable colors, theme saving, highlights , bookmarks, customizable interface, and more.

It loads fast and has additional study tools available for purchase in app as well. You can view a reasonable set of translations and split the view to have up to four bibles side by side. The kjv can be used offline, but others may require the internet.

Has a great search function that works well. iCloud backup of notes, highlights, etc. Overall, it is my favorite bible app by far on iOS. The developer is very good with communication and support as well.

My only desire would be a "slightly" more advanced reading plan. It is simple and works well, but being able to pick a start date would be ideal (I don't always start a plan on January 1), and other apps have far more options. However, for what I use the app for, mainly a very readable and clean and book-like bible experience, the app absolutely excels. I can use other apps for a reading plan (such as ReadingPlan, which can launch this app for readings and is almost the equivalent awesomeness for a reading plan app).

Highly recommend this app. For actually reading the Bible, there is no better kjv app. Period.

I was surprised and saddened to see the poor reviews due to bugs in this latest release, most of which disappeared after the first week or so if you look at the dates. It seems to me that people who have used and loved the App for years, as I have, should have learned something of the virtue of patience and that the proper way to resolve an issue with someone, especially an 'old friend,' is to talk to them rather than ditch them. In my book these behaviors translate to App Reviewing by doing things like hitting App Support instead of Write a Review to report a bug or to ask about a new feature (after reading the tutorial/release notes/etc) in a new release, and then giving him a few days. 
Sure you want to give an honest review, but wouldn't it be nicer to say, "I've used it for years and love it. I use it for ....... This has a bug as of the last release but the author assured me it would be fixed soon. Or, "I preferred it when it worked this way .... But I talked to the author and he had many requests to change it this new way...... Still not my favorite." I guess my expectations are higher for reviews submitted about a Bible App, especially by people who claim to study it. If you read this far, thank you, God Bless, and do try the App!
